content.text:
View A contains four unspecified objects (no identified colors or shapes). Attention is currently concentrated on the left location; the upper and lower locations are barely selected and the right location is effectively unattended. The upper and lower objects are the most recoverable immediately, the left object is moderately recoverable now, and the right object is the least recoverable; recoverability for every object falls with one and two unattended steps. Predicted outcomes of commands are strongly self-reinforcing: issuing a command targeting any location overwhelmingly keeps selection at that same location, so the system shows little ability to reallocate attention across locations in this view.

View B also contains four unspecified objects. Attention is currently concentrated on the lower location; the left and upper locations are weakly selected and the right location is essentially unattended. The right object is the most recoverable now, the left and lower are moderately recoverable, and the upper is the least recoverable; recoverability declines after one and two steps. Command predictions strongly favor moving or keeping selection at the left when commands are issued, so redirecting attention is limited and will largely shift or remain at the left rather than freely choose other locations.
